topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how local treatments remove or destroy tumours and why their success depends on tumour accessibility and extent.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the effectiveness and limitations of killing cancer cells with broadly damaging drugs.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking required hormonal signals can suppress breast and prostate cancer growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing checkpoint proteins create vulnerabilities that can make cancer cells selectively susceptible to treatment.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting one DNA repair pathway selectively kills cancer cells already deficient in another.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the rationale for identifying cancer-driving oncogenes and inhibiting the activated kinases on which tumours depend.

topics.label: Limitations and resistance in kinase inhibitor treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibition often becomes long-term disease management rather than a cure.

topics.label: Antibody-directed cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognising cancer-associated surface proteins direct therapeutic effects toward tumour cells.

topics.label: Antitumour immunity and immune checkpoint blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that endogenous T cells can recognise tumours and that releasing immune checkpoints can strengthen their antitumour response.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells toward cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapies that deliberately give T cells access to cancer-associated targets rather than relying on their existing tumour recognition.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and personalised cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how matching treatment to individual tumours can address variable responses and treatment resistance.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic evaluates improving cancer outcomes in light of changes in prevention and detection as well as treatment.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how future cancer treatment should advance when therapeutic benefit must be weighed against toxicity and the risks of replacing successful existing regimens.
